newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand to gain in merger - Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand to gain in merger - Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Shareholders in Storebrand ASA, Norway's largest insurer, stand to gain the most from the proposed merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA, Norway's second largest bank, according to Merrill Lynch.
In a market update, the investment bank also said it was reinstating coverage of Christiania Bank with a neutral rating.

"We believe that the merger would benefit Storebrand's shareholders more than Christiania's given the former's relatively weak balance sheet and the fact that the Storebrand dividend will now be paid one year earlier," the report, dated April 10, said.
Christiania and Storebrand announced the merger plans on April 2, saying the new company, Christiania Group, would have a market capitalisation of 26 billion crowns.
Each set of shareholders would hold 50 percent of the combined Christiania Group.
It would be the second largest listed company on the Oslo Stock exchange after industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA.
The merger, if approved by shareholders and authorities, would form the country's largest financial group -- larger than DnB -- and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.
